record.title: Sárközy's cycle partition conjecture for edge-colored graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a $t$-colored graph, and let $\alpha(G)$ denote its independence number. Let the cycle partition number be the minimum number of vertex-disjoint monochromatic cycles covering $V(G)$. **Sárközy's conjecture.** The cycle partition number of any $t$-colored graph $G$ is

$$
t\alpha(G).
$$

The statement is known for $t=1$ and is best possible for $t=2$, but Pokrovskiy's example shows that it is false for every $t\geq3$.
record.source_name: Jozsef Balogh, Janos Barat, Daniel Gerbner, Andras Gyarfas and GAbor N. Sarkozy, “Partitioning 2-edge-colored graphs by monochromatic paths and cycles”, arXiv:1509.05544 (2015).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2015). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1509.05539](https://arxiv.org/abs/1509.05539).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1509.05544

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of September 2015). “Then again the counterexample of Pokrovskiy shows that the conjecture is not true in this form for any $t\geq 3$.”

record.title: Ryser–Lovász conjecture for monochromatic tree covers
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $r\text{-}
obreak\text{colorings}$ denote edge-colorings of $G$ with $r$ colors, and let $\mathrm{tc}_r(G)$ be the minimum number of monochromatic connected subgraphs whose vertex sets cover $V(G)$ in every such coloring. Let $alpha(G)$ be the independence number of $G$.

**Ryser–Lovász conjecture.** For every integer $r\geq 2$ and every graph $G$,

$$
\mathrm{tc}_r(G)\leq (r-1)\alpha(G).
$$

The conjecture is best possible when $r-1$ is a prime power. It is known for $r=2,3$ and for complete graphs when $r\leq 5$, but remains open for $r\geq 4$ in general.
record.source_name: Deepak Bal and Louis DeBiasio, “Partitioning random graphs into monochromatic components”, arXiv:1509.09168 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1509.09168

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2015).

record.title: Random-graph tree-cover threshold conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G(n,p)$ be the binomial random graph, and let $\mathrm{tp}_r(G(n,p))$ be the minimum number of monochromatic trees needed to partition the vertex set in every $r$-edge-coloring. Here, “a.a.s.” means with probability tending to one as $n\to\infty$.

**Random-graph tree-cover threshold conjecture.** For every $\epsilon>0$ and every $r\geq 1$, if

$$
p\geq \left(\frac{(1+\epsilon)r\log n}{n}\right)^{1/r},
$$

then a.a.s.

$$
\mathrm{tp}_r(G(n,p))\leq r.
$$

This conjecture aims to identify the sharp threshold for monochromatic tree partitions in random graphs. The $r=2$ case was proved by Kohayakawa, Mota, and Schacht while the general case remains open.
record.source_name: Deepak Bal and Louis DeBiasio, “Partitioning random graphs into monochromatic components”, arXiv:1509.09168 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1509.09168

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2015).

record.title: Maximum-order conjecture for extendable actions on minimal graphs
record.statement:
Let $M_g$ denote the maximum order of an extendable finite group action on a minimal graph of genus $g$. Assume that $g$ is neither a square number nor one of the finitely many values listed in the preceding table. If $g$ is prime, then

$$
M_g=4(g+1).
$$

If $g$ is composite, write $g=pq$, where $p$ is the smallest nontrivial divisor of $g$. Then

$$
M_g=4(p+1)(q+1).
$$

**Maximum-order conjecture.** Under these hypotheses, $M_g$ has the values specified above. The claim concerns the still-unknown maximum orders of extendable finite group actions on minimal graphs, contrasting with the determined maximum orders for arbitrary graphs.
record.source_name: Chao Wang, Shicheng Wang, Yimu Zhang and Bruno Zimmermann, “Graphs in the 3–sphere with maximum symmetry”, arXiv:1510.00822 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1510.00822

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2015).

record.title: Set-coloured complete-graph tree-cover conjecture
record.statement:
Let $K_n$ be the complete graph on $n$ vertices. In an $(r,k)$-colouring, each edge receives a $k$-element subset of a set of $r$ colours; let $\operatorname{tc}_{r,k}(K_n)$ be the minimum number of monochromatic trees needed to cover every such colouring. **Set-coloured tree-cover conjecture.** For all $n\geq 1$ and $r>k\geq 1$,

$$
\operatorname{tc}_{r,k}(K_n)\leq r-k.
$$

The claim follows from Gyárfás's conjecture if that conjecture holds, and is known in several ranges, including $k>r/2$ and $k\geq r/2-1$; later work cited in the source proves it for $k>r/4$. It is not tight in general, as shown by $\operatorname{tc}_{5,2}(K_n)=2$ for $n\geq4$, and remains open in full generality.
record.source_name: Sebastián Bustamante and Maya Stein, “Monochromatic tree covers and Ramsey numbers for set-coloured graphs”, arXiv:1510.05190 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1510.05190

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2015).

record.title: Chen–Fujita–Gyárfás–Lehel–Tóth bipartite tree-cover conjecture
record.statement:
Let $K_{n,m}$ be a complete bipartite graph, and let $\operatorname{tc}_{r,1}(K_{n,m})$ denote the minimum number of monochromatic trees needed to cover every $r$-colouring of its edges. **Chen–Fujita–Gyárfás–Lehel–Tóth conjecture.** If $r>1$, then

$$
\operatorname{tc}_{r,1}(K_{n,m})\leq 2r-2
$$

for all $n,m\geq1$. This is the complete-bipartite analogue of the tree-cover problem, and the source presents the bound as a conjecture without giving a resolution.
record.source_name: Sebastián Bustamante and Maya Stein, “Monochromatic tree covers and Ramsey numbers for set-coloured graphs”, arXiv:1510.05190 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1510.05190

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2015).

record.title: The k-optimal set covering conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph and let $D$ be a **$k$-optimal set**, as defined in the source. A subgraph $M$ of $G$ is **$k$-edge-colorable** if its edges can be colored with $k$ colors so that adjacent edges receive different colors. Write $d_M(v)$ for the degree of $v$ in $M$.

**The k-optimal set covering conjecture.** If $D$ is a $k$-optimal set in $G$, then $G$ has a $k$-edge-colorable subgraph $M$ such that

$$
d_M(v)=k \quad\text{for all }v\in V(G)-D.
$$

This generalizes the stated $k=1$ consequence of Berge's theorem, where a maximum independent set has a matching covering every vertex outside it. The source gives no resolution evidence, so the conjecture is recorded as open.
record.source_name: Gregory J. Puleo, “Maximal k-Edge-Colorable Subgraphs, Vizing's Theorem, and Tuza's Conjecture”, arXiv:1510.07017 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1510.07017

record.title: Subquadratic maximum running time conjecture for graph bootstrap percolation
record.statement:
For $r\geqslant 5$, let $M_r(n)$ denote the maximum number of time steps for which the $K_r$-bootstrap process on $n$ vertices can run before stabilizing. **Subquadratic running-time conjecture.** For all $r\geqslant 5$,

$$
M_r(n)=o(n^2).
$$

The exact maximum running time is unknown for $r\geqslant 5$, and even proving any non-trivial upper bound on $M_r(n)$ is open. The conjecture gives a weaker proposed bound than the heuristic estimate discussed immediately beforehand.
record.source_name: Béla Bollobás, Michał Przykucki, Oliver Riordan and Julian Sahasrabudhe, “On the maximum running time in graph bootstrap percolation”, arXiv:1510.07096 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1510.07096

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2015).

record.title: The eventual exactness conjecture for the lower bound q(n)
record.statement:
Let $[n]=\{1,2,\ldots,n\}$, and let $M(n)$ denote the maximum size of a union-free family of subsets of $[n]$. Let $q(n)$ be the lower-bound function for $M(n)$ constructed in the paper. **Eventual exactness conjecture.** There exists a positive integer $N$ such that

$$
M(n)=\lvert q(n)\rvert
$$

for every positive integer $n>N$. This is the stronger eventual form of the preceding conjecture, asserting that the lower bound is attained for all sufficiently large $n$.
record.source_name: Andy Loo, “Union-Free Families of Subsets”, arXiv:1511.00170 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1511.00170

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2015).

record.title: Extremal maximal-matchings conjecture for benzenoid chains
record.statement:
Let $B_n$ be a benzenoid chain of length $n$, and let $H_n$ denote the helicene benzenoid chain of length $n$. For a graph $G$, write $Psi(G)$ for its number of maximal matchings.

**Extremal maximal-matchings conjecture.** For every benzenoid chain $B_n$ of length $n$,

$$
\Psi(H_n) \leq \Psi(B_n).
$$

The conjecture asserts that the helicene has the smallest number of maximal matchings among all benzenoid chains of the same length. The surrounding discussion presents this as an unresolved extremal problem and notes that maximal matchings appear to decrease as the number of kinky hexagons increases, while their value may also depend on the direction of successive turns.
record.source_name: Tomislav Došlić and Taylor Short, “Maximal matchings in polyspiro and benzenoid chains”, arXiv:1511.00590 (2015).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1511.00590

record.title: The rational-point invariance conjecture for tropical linear series
record.statement: Let $\Delta$ be a tropical complex and let $D$ be a Weil divisor on $\Delta$. Define $h^0(\Delta,D)$ as the smallest cardinality of a set of rational points that is not contained in any effective divisor linearly equivalent to $D$, or infinity if no such finite set exists. The conjecture concerns replacing rational points by arbitrary points in this definition. **Rational-point invariance conjecture.** The definition of $h^0$ is equivalent to the analogous definition where the points are allowed to be arbitrary, not necessarily rational, points. This would remove a technical rationality restriction from the definition of $h^0$; the source gives no resolution of the conjecture.
record.source_name: Dustin Cartwright, “A specialization inequality for tropical complexes”, arXiv:1511.00650 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1511.00650

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2015).

record.title: The tangent-developable intersection conjecture for cuspidal projections
record.statement: Let $C_n$ be the rational normal curve in $\mathbb{P}^n$, let $T_n$ be its tangent developable, and let $S_n$ be its secant variety. A **cuspidal projection center** is a projection center $V$ of a projection from $\mathbb{P}^n$ to $\mathbb{P}^2$. **The tangent-developable intersection conjecture.** If $V$ intersects neither $C_n$ nor $S_n$ outside $T_n$, then $V$ intersects $T_n$ in at most three points for every $n\geq4$ with $n\neq5$; for $n=5$, the maximum number of intersection points is four. This is proposed as a projection-theoretic analogue of the cusp bound, and the source gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Torgunn Karoline Moe, “Rational Cuspidal Curves”, arXiv:1511.02691 (2015).
record.references:

record.title: The saturation conjecture for additive polynomial mappings
record.statement:
Let $K$ be the global function field in the setup, let $F\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb{F}_p}(\mathbb{G}_{a/K}^d)$ be an additive polynomial mapping, and let $\kappa$ and $\delta$ denote its saturation and dynamic degrees. **Saturation conjecture.** (i) If no non-zero proper connected algebraic subgroup of $\mathbb{G}_{a/K}^d$ is stable under $F$, then

$$
\kappa=\delta.
$$
 (ii) For a short exact sequence of $t$-modules

$$
0\to H\to G\to G/H\to0,
$$

 the invariant satisfies

$$
\kappa(G)^{\dim G}=\kappa(H)^{\dim H}\kappa(G/H)^{\dim(G/H)}.
$$

The conjecture is intended to determine the saturation invariant for all $t$-modules; the source presents it as unproved and likely relevant to the preceding strengthening of the main theorem.
record.source_name: Vesselin Dimitrov, “Silverman's conjecture for additive polynomial mappings”, arXiv:1511.04061 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1511.04061

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2015).

record.title: The large-clique conjecture for graphs excluding a complete minor
record.statement:
Let $\textup{cliques}(n,t,k)$ denote the maximum number of $k$-cliques in an $n$-vertex graph with no $K_t$-minor. **Large-clique conjecture.** There are constants $c_1,c_2>0$ such that, for all integers $t\geq 3$, $k\geq c_1\log t$, and $n\geq t-1$,

$$
\textup{cliques}(n,t,k)\leq (c_2t)^k n.
$$

For fixed $k$, the quantity is known up to a constant factor of order $(t\sqrt{\log t})^{k-1}n$, while the conjectured bound is known for sufficiently large $k$, leaving the intermediate range open.
record.source_name: David R. Wood, “Cliques in Graphs Excluding a Complete Graph Minor”, arXiv:1511.04655 (2016).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1511.04655

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2015).

record.title: The very-large-clique conjecture for graphs excluding a complete minor
record.statement:
Let $\textup{cliques}(n,t,k)$ denote the maximum number of $k$-cliques in an $n$-vertex graph with no $K_t$-minor. **Very-large-clique conjecture.** There is some $\lambda\in[\tfrac13,1)$ such that, for all integers $t\geq 3$, $k\geq\lambda t$, and $n\geq t-1$,

$$
\textup{cliques}(n,t,k)\leq \binom{t-2}{k-1}\left(n-\frac{(k-1)(t-1)}{k}\right).
$$

This conjecture asserts that the lower bound established earlier is tight for cliques whose size is a fixed positive fraction of $t$. The source presents it as open; it concerns the extremal regime of very large cliques in $K_t$-minor-free graphs.
record.source_name: David R. Wood, “Cliques in Graphs Excluding a Complete Graph Minor”, arXiv:1511.04655 (2016).

record.title: Minimization version of the union-closed sets conjecture
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a union-closed family with nonempty set collection $\mathcal{S}(\mathcal{F})$, and let $m(\mathcal{F})$ be its number of sets and $a(\mathcal{F})$ the maximum number of sets containing a single element. For any positive integer $m$, define

$$
\mathscr{G}(m)=\{\mathcal{F}\mid \mathcal{F}\textup{ is a union-closed family},\ \mathcal{S}(\mathcal{F})\neq \emptyset\textup{ and }m(\mathcal{F})=m\}.
$$

**Minimization conjecture.** For all $m\in\mathbb{N}^+$,

$$
\min_{\mathcal{F}\in\mathscr{G}(m)}a(\mathcal{F})\geq\frac{m}{2}.
$$

This is the companion optimization formulation of Frankl's conjecture. The paper presents it as a new conjecture with computational support and special cases, but it remains open.
record.source_name: Jonad Pulaj, Annie Raymond and Dirk Theis, “New Conjectures for Union-Closed Families”, arXiv:1512.00083 (2016).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1512.00083

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2015).

record.title: The f-conjecture for union-closed families
record.statement:
Let $f(n,a)$ denote the optimization quantity defined in the paper for union-closed families on $n$ ground-set elements with maximum element frequency at most $a$. **$f$-conjecture.** For fixed $a\in\mathbb{N}^+$, one has

$$
f(n,a)=f(n+1,a)
$$

for every $n\in\mathbb{N}^+$ satisfying $n\geq\lceil\log_2 a\rceil+1$. The conjecture asserts stabilization of this quantity as the ground-set size increases; the paper gives computational evidence, but no general proof is supplied.
record.source_name: Jonad Pulaj, Annie Raymond and Dirk Theis, “New Conjectures for Union-Closed Families”, arXiv:1512.00083 (2016).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1512.00083

record.title: Unique non-Markov measure maximizing ascendancy on the golden mean shift
record.statement: Let the golden mean shift be the shift space on two symbols in which the block $11$ is forbidden, and let $\nu$ range over all invariant probability measures on it. Write $\operatorname{Asc}_{\nu}$ for measure-theoretic ascendancy. A measure is **Markov of order $k$** when its conditional probabilities depend only on the preceding $k$ symbols. **Non-Markov maximizer conjecture.** On the golden mean shift there is a unique measure of maximum $\operatorname{Asc}_{\mu}$, and it is not Markov of any order. The source offers this as a conjectural extrapolation beyond finite-order Markov measures and gives no resolution, so the conjecture remains open.
record.source_name: Karl Petersen and Benjamin Wilson, “Dynamical intricacy and average sample complexity”, arXiv:1512.01143 (2016).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1512.01143

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2015).

record.title: Conjecture on uniform cutset sizes in the truncated Boolean lattice
record.statement:
Let $g_n(m,l)$ denote the minimum size of a cutset in the truncated Boolean lattice with parameters $n$, $m$, and $l$. For $n\gg m$, the following assertions are conjectured.

**Uniform cutset conjecture.**

$$
g_n(m,l)=\binom{n}{m}-\binom{n}{m-1}
$$

for every $l=2m,2m+1,\dots,n-m-1$, and

$$
g_n(m,n-m)=\binom{n-1}{m}-\binom{n-1}{m-1}.
$$

These claims describe the observed stabilization of $g_n(m,l)$ across the middle range of levels and its separate value at the endpoint $l=n-m$. The condition $n\gg m$ is informal in the source, and the conjectural formulas are not established there.
record.source_name: Béla Bajnok and Shahriar Shahriari, “On Uniform f-vectors of Cutsets in the Truncated Boolean Lattice”, arXiv:1512.02973 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1512.02973

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2015).

record.title: Conjectural formula for restricted sumsets in cyclic groups
record.statement:
Let $\mathbb{Z}_n$ be the cyclic group of order $n$. For an $m$-subset of $\mathbb{Z}_n$, let $\rho\hat{\;} (\mathbb{Z}_n,m,h)$ denote the minimum size of its restricted $h$-fold sumset. Let $u(n,m,h)$ be the previously defined lower-bound function, and let $w\hat{\;} (n,m,h)$ be the minimum, over divisors $d$ of $n$, of the restricted sumset sizes arising from the two-partial-coset construction $B_d(n,m)$. **Bajnok's restricted-sumset formula conjecture.** For all $n$, $m$, and $h$,

$$
\rho\hat{\;} (\mathbb{Z}_n,m,h)=\min\{u(n,m,h),w\hat{\;} (n,m,h)\}.
$$

The formula incorporates the standard coset construction and the exceptional two-partial-coset constructions known to improve it; all known exceptions arise from those cases, but equality is not proved in general.
record.source_name: Béla Bajnok, “Open problems about sumsets in finite abelian groups: minimum sizes and critical numbers”, arXiv:1512.03038 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1512.03038

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2015).

record.title: Restricted sumset formula for the small-set regime
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite abelian group of order $n$, let $p$ be the smallest prime divisor of $n$, and let $\rho\hat{\;} (G,m,h)$ denote the minimum restricted $h$-fold sumset size among $m$-subsets of $G$. **Small-set restricted-sumset conjecture.** If $h<m\leq p$, then

$$
\rho\hat{\;} (G,m,h)=\min\{p,hm-h^2+1\}.
$$

This extends the prime-order restricted sumset formula of Dias da Silva and Hamidoune to the stated small-set regime in arbitrary finite abelian groups; the source presents it as conjectural.
record.source_name: Béla Bajnok, “Open problems about sumsets in finite abelian groups: minimum sizes and critical numbers”, arXiv:1512.03038 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1512.03038

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2015).

record.title: Bound on the number of exceptional restricted double-sumset sizes
record.statement:
Let $G$ be an abelian group of order $n$, and let $\rho_{\pm}(G,m,2)$ and $\rho(G,m,2)$ denote the minimum signed and unrestricted double sumset sizes of an $m$-subset of $G$. **Bajnok and Matzke's exceptional-value bound.** The two quantities disagree for fewer than $n/4$ values of $m$.

$$
\#\{m: \rho_{\pm}(G,m,2)\neq\rho(G,m,2)\}<\frac n4.
$$

The source notes that the exact count is $(p-1)^2/4$ for the treated rank-two elementary abelian case and conjectures the stated universal bound for all finite abelian groups.
record.source_name: Béla Bajnok, “Open problems about sumsets in finite abelian groups: minimum sizes and critical numbers”, arXiv:1512.03038 (2017).

record.title: Conjectural formula for unrestricted-length restricted sumsets in cyclic groups
record.statement:
Let $n$ be a positive integer and let $m\leq n$. For an $m$-subset $A$ of $\mathbb{Z}_n$, write $\Sigma A=\bigcup_{h=0}^{\infty}h\hat{\;}A$ for its restricted sumset over all numbers of terms, and let $\rho\hat{\;} (\mathbb{Z}_n,m,\mathbb{N}_0)$ be the minimum possible size of $\Sigma A$. Let $u(n,m,\mathbb{N}_0)$ be the divisor-based function defined from the constructions $C_d(n,m)$. **Unrestricted-length restricted-sumset formula conjecture.** For all positive integers $n$ and $m\leq n$,

$$
\rho\hat{\;} (\mathbb{Z}_n,m,\mathbb{N}_0)=u(n,m,\mathbb{N}_0).
$$

The construction gives the upper bound, and numerical experimentation in the source supports equality; a proof is not supplied.
record.source_name: Béla Bajnok, “Open problems about sumsets in finite abelian groups: minimum sizes and critical numbers”, arXiv:1512.03038 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1512.03038

record.title: Jang–Kim's maximal norm conjecture for indecomposable integers
record.statement:
Let $D$ be a positive nonsquare integer, let $\mathbb Z[\sqrt D]$ be the quadratic order, and let $N$ be the minimum of the absolute values of negative norms of elements of $\mathbb Z[\sqrt D]$. Let $a$ be the smallest nonnegative rational integer such that $N$ divides $D-a^2$. An element of $\mathbb Z[\sqrt D]$ is **indecomposable** if it cannot be written as a sum of two totally positive elements. **Jang–Kim's conjecture.** For every indecomposable $\alpha\in\mathbb Z[\sqrt D]$, one has

$$
N(\alpha)\leq \frac{D-a^2}{N}.
$$

The conjecture proposed an improvement of the general bound $N(\alpha)\leq D/N$ for indecomposable integers. It is false in the quadratic field considered in the paper, so the proposed bound does not hold in general.
record.source_name: Vítězslav Kala, “Norms of indecomposable integers in real quadratic fields”, arXiv:1512.04691 (2016).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1512.04691

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of December 2015).

record.title: Lehel–Puleo conjecture on triangle-independent sets and bipartite deletion
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a simple undirected graph on $n$ vertices. A **triangle-independent set** is an edge set containing at most one edge from each triangle of $G$. Let $\tau_{B}(G)$ be the minimum number of edges whose deletion makes $G$ bipartite, and let $\alpha_{1}(G)$ be the maximum size of a triangle-independent set. **Lehel–Puleo conjecture.** For every $n$-vertex graph $G$,

$$
\alpha_{1}(G)+\tau_{B}(G)\leq \frac{n^2}{4}.
$$

This is stronger than the Erdős–Gallai–Tuza conjecture because $\tau_{B}(G)\geq\tau_{1}(G)$. The conjecture is attributed independently to Lehel and Puleo; its status is not resolved in the supplied source.
record.source_name: Honghai Xu, “A Note on Bipartite Subgraphs and Triangle-independent Sets”, arXiv:1512.06202 (2016).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1512.06202

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2015).

record.title: Tohaneanu–Van Tuyl degree-one minimum-distance conjecture for complete intersections
record.statement:
Let $\mathbb{X}$ be a finite set of points in $\mathbb{P}^{s-1}$, and let $I(\mathbb{X})$ be a complete intersection generated by $f_1,\ldots,f_{s-1}$. Set $e_i=\deg(f_i)$ and assume

$$
2\leq e_i\leq e_{i+1}\quad\text{for all }i.
$$

Write $\delta_{\mathbb{X}}(1)$ for the minimum distance in degree one. **Tohaneanu–Van Tuyl's conjecture.** One has

$$
\delta_{\mathbb{X}}(1)\geq (e_1-1)e_2\cdots e_{s-1}.
$$

The conjecture concerns the degree-one minimum distance of projective complete-intersection point sets and is presented as a result resembling the nested-cartesian conjecture in the special case $d=1$. Its resolution status is not specified in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Jose Martinez-Bernal, Yuriko Pitones and Rafael H. Villarreal, “Minimum distance functions of graded ideals and Reed-Muller-type codes”, arXiv:1512.06868 (2016).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1512.06868

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2015).

record.title: Herbrand consistency search form of the TFNP conjecture
record.statement: Let $\mathcal T$ be the class of theories under consideration. For a consistent universal sentence $\Phi$, let $HCS(\Phi)$ be its Herbrand Consistency Search problem: given finitely many tuples of terms, find a truth assignment to the relevant atomic subformulas making the corresponding instances of $\Phi$ true. **Herbrand consistency search TFNP conjecture.** For every $T\in\mathcal T$, there exists a consistent universal sentence $\Phi$ such that $HCS(\Phi)$ is not polynomially reducible to any TFNP problem provably total in $T$, equivalently $HCS(\Phi)\notin\operatorname{TFNP}^*(T)$. This is an equivalent Herbrand-search formulation of the TFNP conjecture.
record.source_name: Pavel Pudlak, “Incompleteness in the finite domain”, arXiv:1601.01487 (2017).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2010–2016). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1008.0225](https://arxiv.org/abs/1008.0225).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1601.01487

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2016).

record.title: Additivity of nonnegative rank under Cartesian products
record.statement:
Let $P_1$ and $P_2$ be polytopes. Their **nonnegative rank** is the smallest number of nonnegative factors in a nonnegative factorization of a slack matrix of the polytope. **Product additivity conjecture.** The nonnegative rank is additive under Cartesian products:

$$
\mathrm{rk}_+(P_1 \times P_2)=\mathrm{rk}_+(P_1)+\mathrm{rk}_+(P_2).
$$

This conjecture would describe how nonnegative rank behaves under direct sums of matroids, since direct sums correspond to Cartesian products of matroid base polytopes. It was first asked during a Dagstuhl seminar in 2013; the source gives no resolution.

record.title: Generalised Thue chromatic index bound for Jaco graphs
record.statement:
Let $J^{\ast}_n(f(x))$ be a Jaco graph, where

$$
f(x)=mx+c,
$$

with $x\in\mathbb{N}$, $m\geq 2$, and $c\geq 1$. Write $\pi(J^{\ast}_n(f(x)))$ for its Thue chromatic index, and let $\Delta(J^{\ast}_n(f(x)))$ and $\delta(J^{\ast}_n(f(x)))$ denote its maximum and minimum degrees, respectively.

**Generalised Jaco graph conjecture.** For every such Jaco graph,

$$
\pi(J^{\ast}_n(f(x)))\leq \Delta(J^{\ast}_n(f(x)))+\delta(J^{\ast}_n(f(x))).
$$

This conjecture generalises the preceding bound for the considered Jaco graphs by relating the Thue chromatic index to both the maximum and minimum degrees. The source provides no resolution, so the conjecture remains open.

record.title: Li–Magnant proper connection conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected noncomplete graph with $n$ vertices, where $n\geq 5$, and let $\delta(G)$ denote its minimum degree. **Li–Magnant's proper connection conjecture.** Then

$$
pc(G)=2.
$$

This conjecture proposes that the sharp minimum-degree threshold $\delta(G)\geq n/4$ guarantees a proper connection number of two, extending the known result that requires $n\geq 68$. Its resolution is the subject of the source paper.

record.title: The ultimate Elekes–Rónyai theorem for rational functions
record.statement:
Let $f\in\mathbb C(x,y)$ be a rational function of degree $d$, where the degree is the maximum of the degrees of its numerator and denominator after removing common factors. Call $f$ **additive** if it has the form $g(h(x)+k(y))$, and **multiplicative** if it has the form $g(h(x)\cdot k(y))$, with rational functions in the relevant variables. **The ultimate Elekes–Rónyai conjecture.** If $f$ is not additive or multiplicative, then for all $A,B\subset\mathbb C$ with $|A|=|B|=n$,

$$
|f(A\times B)|=\Omega_{d,\varepsilon}(n^{2-\varepsilon}).
$$

This extends the polynomial expansion problem to rational functions and predicts an almost quadratic image; it remains open in the survey.

record.title: The cubic graph upper-bound conjecture for rainbow-free $P_4$ colorings
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected cubic graph of order $n$. Here, $W^+(G; K_2,P_4)$ denotes the maximum number of colors in a vertex coloring of $G$ with no monochromatic or rainbow copy of $K_2$ or $P_4$.

**Cubic graph upper-bound conjecture.**

$$
W^+(G; K_2,P_4)\le n/2+1,
$$

with equality exactly when $G$ is bipartite.

Computer evidence suggests this bound. The value $n/2+1$ is attained for all bipartite graphs by the cited observations and the fact that regular bipartite graphs have perfect matchings; the conjectured upper bound for connected cubic graphs remains open.

record.title: Diameter conjecture for pointihedra
record.statement:
Let $P$ be a convex $n$-gon with $n\geq 13$, and let $P^{\text{\raisebox{1px}{\scalebox{0.7}{$\star$}}}}$ be the resulting polygon with a puncture placed in its interior. Write ${\overline{\mathcal F}}(P^{\text{\raisebox{1px}{\scalebox{0.7}{$\star$}}}})$ for the pointihedron flip-graph and ${\rm diam}$ for graph diameter. **Diameter conjecture.** For some placement of the puncture in the interior of $P$,

$$
{\rm diam}({\overline{\mathcal F}}(P^{\text{\raisebox{1px}{\scalebox{0.7}{$\star$}}}}))=2n-7.
$$

Earlier results in the paper give bounds on the diameter of these flip-graphs; this conjecture proposes the exact value $2n-7$ for a suitable placement when $n\geq 13$.

record.title: Uniqueness of the local maximum of the aerial-base-station coverage function
record.statement:
Let $\gamma$ be a QoS requirement and let $f_c$ be an operating frequency. For the propagation environments whose parameters are listed in Table 1, define

$$
\Gamma(\alpha) = \frac{10^{\frac{\gamma-(A P(\alpha)+B)}{10}}}{1+\alpha^2},
$$

where $\alpha\in[0,\infty]$ and $P(\alpha)$ is the propagation-model function. **Uniqueness conjecture.** For any $\gamma$ and $f_c$, if a local maximum exists for $\Gamma(\alpha)$, then it is the only local maximum of $\Gamma(\alpha)$ on $[0,\infty]$ for each of the listed propagation environments. The uniqueness of this maximum would justify selecting the optimal elevation-to-coverage-radius ratio by one-dimensional maximization of $\Gamma(\alpha)$, although the statement is presented without a proof in the source.

record.title: Pippinger's inducibility conjecture for cycles
record.statement:
Let $C_k$ denote the cycle on $k$ vertices. For a graph $H$, its induced density is the number of induced copies of $H$ divided by $\binom{|G|}{|H|}$; write $I(H;n)$ for the maximum induced density of $H$ over graphs $G$ on $n$ vertices, and call $\lim_{n\to\infty} I(H;n)$ the **inducibility** of $H$. **Pippinger's conjecture.** For $k\ge 5$, the inducibility of the cycle $C_k$ is

$$
\frac{k!}{k^k-k}.
$$

This conjecture, posed by Pippinger and Golumbic in 1975, concerns the extremal induced density of fixed cycles. Apart from the case resolved in the paper, the problem remains open; see the cited work for results on the inducibility of other graphs.
record.source_name: Natasha Morrison and Alex Scott, “Maximising the number of induced cycles in a graph”, arXiv:1603.02960 (2017).

record.title: Kowalik–Lużar–Skrekovski conjecture for planar graphs of girth at least five
record.statement:
A **feedback vertex set** of a graph $G$ is a set $S\subseteq V(G)$ such that $G-S$ is a forest. Let $\phi(G)$ denote the minimum size of a feedback vertex set of $G$. The **girth** of a graph is the length of its shortest cycle, with girth infinity for an acyclic graph. **Kowalik–Lużar–Skrekovski conjecture.** If $G$ is a planar graph of girth at least five on $n$ vertices, then

$$
\phi(G)\leq\frac{3n}{10}.
$$

The bound is tight because the dodecahedron attains it. The supplied text does not state a resolution of this conjecture; the source paper presents it as an active problem and develops improved bounds toward it.

record.title: Gustavsson–Nash-Williams conjecture on clique decompositions
record.statement:
Let $r\ge 3$. A graph $G$ is **$K_r$-divisible** when its number of edges is divisible by $\binom{r}{2}$ and every vertex degree is divisible by $r-1$.

**Gustavsson–Nash-Williams conjecture.** For every $r\ge 3$, there exists an $n_0=n_0(r)$ such that every $K_r$-divisible graph $G$ on $n\ge n_0$ vertices with

$$
\delta(G)\ge (1-1/(r+1))n
$$
\nhas a $K_r$-decomposition.

This conjecture predicts the asymptotically sharp minimum-degree threshold for decomposing divisible graphs into copies of a clique. It is attributed to Nash-Williams for triangles and to Gustavsson in general; the supplied source gives no resolution status.

record.title: Plummer–Toft conjecture on cyclic coloring of 3-connected plane graphs
record.statement: Let $G$ be a $3$-connected plane graph, and let $Delta^\star$ be its maximum face size. A **cyclic coloring** of $G$ is a vertex coloring in which any two vertices incident with the same face receive distinct colors. **Plummer–Toft's conjecture.** Every $3$-connected plane graph with maximum face size $\Delta^\star$ has a cyclic coloring with at most $\Delta^\star+2$ colors. The conjecture is known for $\Delta^\star=3$, $\Delta^\star=4$, and $\Delta^\star\ge 18$, and this paper proves the cases $\Delta^\star=16$ and $\Delta^\star=17$; the remaining values are not resolved here.

record.title: The point-circle incidence bound conjecture
record.statement:
Let $P$ be a set of $n$ points in the Euclidean plane, and let $c_k$ denote the maximum number of circles containing at least $k$ points of $P$. **Point-circle incidence bound conjecture.** For every $\varepsilon>0$ and $k>n^\varepsilon$,

$$
c_k=O(n^2k^{-3}+nk^{-1}).
$$

The paper states that this bound, together with the conjectured bisector-energy estimate, would yield nearly tight bounds for its distinct-bisector and pinned-distance theorems.

record.title: Straub's largest-size conjecture for odd $(s,s+2)$-core partitions
record.statement:
Let $s$ be an odd positive integer. An $(s,s+2)$-core partition is a partition that is simultaneously an $s$-core and an $(s+2)$-core, and its parts are required to be distinct. **Straub's conjecture.** The largest size of an $(s,s+2)$-core partition into distinct parts is

$$
\frac{(s^2-1)(s+3)(5s+17)}{384}.
$$

Straub posed this conjecture in the study of simultaneous core partitions; the surrounding paper focuses on the number and largest size of $(2k+1,2k+3)$-core partitions into distinct parts and states that it verifies the two conjectures mentioned. The supplied text does not explicitly give a resolution status for this individual claim, so it is recorded as open.

record.title: The covering-product lower-bound conjecture for convex bodies
record.statement:
For a convex body $K\in\mathcal{K}^n$, let $\mu_i(K)$ denote its $i$th covering minimum. **Covering-product lower-bound conjecture.** For every $K\in\mathcal{K}^n$,

$$
\mu_1(K)\cdots\mu_n(K)\operatorname{vol}(K)\geq\frac{n+1}{2^n},
$$

with equality, for example, for

$$
T_n=\operatorname{conv}\{e_1,\ldots,e_n,-\mathbf{1}\}.
$$

The conjecture seeks the sharp lower bound for the covering product; the paper notes that its value should decay exponentially with dimension and verifies the bound in dimension two and for important classes of bodies, while the general case remains open.

record.title: Containment of the amenable radical in random-walk stabilizers
record.statement: Let $G$ be a finitely generated group, and let $\boldsymbol{A_\mu}$ be the subgroup associated with a symmetric, aperiodic probability measure $\mu$ on $G$ whose support generates $G$. The **amenable radical** is the largest amenable normal subgroup of $G$. **Amenable-radical containment conjecture.** For every such measure $\mu$, the subgroup $A_\mu$ contains the amenable radical of $G$. This would establish that the subgroup detected by the random walk always contains the canonical amenable normal part of the group; the supplied text does not state whether the conjecture is known or remains open.

record.title: Horizontal-line finiteness conjecture for the Rossby wavenumber set
record.statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be the wavenumber set, whose elements are pairs $(a,b)$. For positive $a,b$, consider resonant Rossby waves with fixed meridional wavenumber $b$. **Horizontal-line finiteness conjecture.** If $(a,b)$ is in the wavenumber set $\Lambda$ and $a,b>0$, then

$$
a<\sqrt{3}b^4
$$

unless $(a,b)=(800,4)$. In particular, every horizontal line contains only finitely many points of the wavenumber sets shown in the figures, and only finitely many Rossby waves with fixed meridional wavenumber exhibit nonzonal resonances. This is a numerical conjecture about the anisotropy of the wavenumber set; its resolution is not supplied here.

record.title: Hereditary equality of domination and porous exponential domination
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. For a vertex set $D$ of $G$, define its porous exponential domination weight at $u$ by

$$
w^*_{(G,D)}(u)=\sum_{v\in D}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{\operatorname{dist}_G(u,v)-1}.
$$

The porous exponential domination number $\gamma_e^*(G)$ is the minimum order of a set $D$ satisfying $w^*_{(G,D)}(u)\geq 1$ for every vertex $u$ of $G$. **Hereditary porous-domination equivalence conjecture.** A graph $G$ satisfies $\gamma(H)=\gamma_e(H)$ for every induced subgraph $H$ of $G$ if and only if it satisfies $\gamma(H)=\gamma_e^*(H)$ for every induced subgraph $H$ of $G$. This conjecture compares ordinary exponential domination with its porous variant on all induced subgraphs; the paper gives no resolution.

record.title: Simple 3-partite hypergraph generalization of Drisko's theorem
record.statement:
Let $H$ be a simple $3$-partite hypergraph with sides $A$, $B$, and $C$, where simplicity means that no edge is repeated. Let $\nu(H)$ denote the maximum matching size. **Generalized Drisko conjecture.** If

$$
|A|=2n-1,
$$

$$
\deg(a)\ge n\quad\text{for every }a\in A,
$$

$$
\deg(v)\le 2n-1\quad\text{for every }v\in B\cup C,
$$

then

$$
\nu(H)\ge n.
$$

This is proposed as a simple-hypergraph generalization of the sharp $2n-1$ rainbow matching theorem; its status is not resolved in the supplied text.

record.title: Degree-bounded bipartite rainbow matching conjecture
record.statement:
Let $d>1$, and let $F_1,\ldots,F_k$ be bipartite graphs on a common vertex set. Write $\Delta(F_i)$ for the maximum vertex degree of $F_i$, and call a choice of pairwise vertex-disjoint edges $e_i\in F_i$ a rainbow matching.

**Degree-bounded bipartite rainbow matching conjecture.** If

$$
\Delta(F_i)\leq d\quad\text{and}\quad |F_i|>(k-1)d
$$

for every $i$, then the system $F_1,\ldots,F_k$ has a rainbow matching.

The source notes that the analogous assertion fails for $d=1$, while suggesting that the degree bound $d>1$ should suffice. No resolution is supplied in the source.

record.title: Strong cross-star conjecture for lifted set families
record.statement:
Let $t\geq 1$, let $\mathcal{F}$ be a family, and let $m$ be a positive integer. The notation $\mathcal{S}_{\mathcal{F},m}$ denotes the associated lifted set family, and the **strong cross-$t$-star property** is the property asserted in the conjecture. **Strong cross-star conjecture.** There exists a positive integer $m_0(t)$ such that, for every family $\mathcal{F}$ and every $m\geq m_0(t)$, the pair

$$
(\mathcal{S}_{\mathcal{F},m},\mathcal{S}_{\mathcal{F},m})
$$

has the strong cross-$t$-star property. The paper further conjectures that the smallest possible value is $m_0(t)=t+1$, and that the pair has the extrastrong cross-$t$-star property when $m>t+1$.

record.title: Existence of the limiting distribution of the truncated extremal process
record.statement:
Let $\varrho_{n,n-k}$ denote the point measure of particles at generation $n$ whose most recent common ancestor with the minimum particle is at least $n-k$ generations from the root. A point measure is a measure on the real line that takes values in the nonnegative integers on bounded sets. **Limiting-distribution conjecture.** For every $k\in\mathbb{N}$, there exists a point measure $\varrho_k$ such that

$$
\lim_{n \to \infty} \varrho_{n,n-k}=\varrho_k.
$$

The authors state that they were not able to study this limiting distribution, although they believe that the law probably exists; no resolution is supplied in the source.

record.title: Aouchiche et al. pineapple graph conjecture for spectral radius minus average degree
record.statement: Let $G$ be a connected graph on $n$ vertices. Its spectral radius is the largest eigenvalue of its adjacency matrix, and its average degree is $2|E(G)|/n$. A **pineapple graph** is the graph obtained by joining a clique to a path-like collection of pendant vertices, as used in the source. **Aouchiche et al. conjecture.** The connected graph on $n$ vertices that maximizes the spectral radius minus the average degree is a pineapple graph. The paper states this as a conjecture from 2008 and proves it, identifying the unique extremal graph in the terminology of the source.

record.title: The MMS star conjecture for Latin squares of order 6
record.statement:
A Latin square of order $6$ can be viewed as the corresponding orthogonal-array configuration, with points and lines carrying the induced incidence structure. It has the **MMS star property** when, for every zero-sum weighting of its points, the largest set of nonnegative lines has size at least the size of a star.

**MMS star conjecture for order 6.** Any Latin square of order $6$ has the MMS star property.

The authors state this after noting that they have no examples with a weighting having only $5$ nonnegative lines. The source gives no proof or disproof, so the conjecture remains open.
